# neathack-agent

> Built live during **[neatHack](https://neatlogs.com/hackathon)**, Oct 10–12, 2026. Follow along: **#neatHack**

An AI agent that finishes a substantial task from start to finish, the kind you'd trust to run without watching it.

_The pitch goes here once the idea is locked in._

## Built with

| Tool | How it's used |
|---|---|
| [neatlogs](https://neatlogs.com) | Traces every agent run: LLM and tool calls, retries, latency, tokens and cost. Used to find failures and to prove before/after improvements. |
| [Entire](https://entire.io) | Records the coding-agent session behind every commit in this repo as a checkpoint (see the `Entire-Checkpoint:` commit trailers). |
| [cfo.ai](https://cfo.ai) | The business plan around the agent: pricing, costs, revenue and runway. |
| Python 3.11 + [uv](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/) | Agent runtime. |

## Quickstart

```bash
uv sync
cp .env.example .env              # fill in the keys
uv run python -m agent.smoke      # one traced LLM call; check it in neatlogs
```

## Hackathon evidence

| Requirement | Where |
|---|---|
| Agent improved (before/after neatlogs numbers) | _coming_ |
| neatlogs traces | _coming_ |
| Entire checkpoints | commit trailers + `entire checkpoint list` |
| cfo.ai business plan (pricing, costs, revenue, runway) | _coming_ |
| A failed action and the agent's recovery | _coming_ |
| Built in public (#neatHack posts) | [docs/build-log.md](docs/build-log.md) |
| Code written during the event | this repo's commit history |

entries.name: WebFetch
entries.description:
Fetches a URL, converts the page to markdown, and answers `prompt` against it using a small fast model.

- Fails on authenticated/private URLs — use an authenticated MCP tool or `gh` for those instead. claude.ai artifact links (claude.ai/artifact/{id} or claude.ai/code/artifact/{uuid}) are published artifacts: read them with the Artifact tool (action "read"), not WebFetch or curl.
- Fails on localhost and other hostnames without a dot; for a local server, use curl via Bash.
- HTTP is upgraded to HTTPS. Cross-host redirects are returned to you rather than followed; call again with the redirect URL.
- Responses are cached for 15 minutes per URL.

prompt.description: The prompt to run on the fetched content

offset.description: Character position in the page text to start reading from. Use it to read on through a page too long for one call, with the value the previous result gave.

The estimates vary widely, mostly because publishers define the market differently (hardware only, software only, or services) and use different base years.

**Hardware market, 2025 base:**
- Global Market Insights puts the market at about $11.7 billion in 2025, with a projected $34.2 billion by 2035 and an 11.4% CAGR for 2026–2035 The market is expected to grow from USD 12.9 billion in 2026 to USD 21.8 billion in 2031 & USD 34.2 billion in 2035. That is the high-growth end of the range.
- A different GMI listing of the same market gives $11.7 billion as the 2024 value and a 10.4% CAGR for 2025–2034, with a forecast of $31.4 billion The Global Programmable Logic Controller Market was valued at USD 11.7 billion in 2024 and is projected to grow at a CAGR of 10.4% from 2025 to 2034.. The two GMI editions disagree on the base year and the growth rate, so check which edition you're citing.

**Lower-growth estimates:**
- Technavio's 2025–2029 report forecasts a 3.5% CAGR, and its incremental growth is smaller: the programmable logic controller (PLC) market size is forecast to increase by USD 3.01 billion, at a CAGR of 3.5% between 2024 and 2029.
- Another research firm values the market at USD 12.69 Billion in 2023, with an estimate of USD 13.38 Billion in 2024 to USD 19.29 Billion by 2032, growing at a CAGR of 5.4% over 2025–2032.

**Software-only segment:**
- A Reanin report values PLC software alone at about $3.02 billion in 2025, growing to roughly $4.43 billion by 2032 at a 5.6% CAGR, per its listing valued at USD 3,023.19 million in the year 2025.

**Takeaway:** For a 2025 hardware market figure, around $11.7 billion is the most commonly cited number, with growth forecasts ranging from roughly 3.5% to 11.4% CAGR depending on the publisher. For a defensible figure, use GMI's 2025 value and note the forecast range. Full reports are paywalled, so the methodology and exact scope are worth checking before relying on any single number.

I found no independent, peer-reviewed study with a general percentage. The figures I found come from vendor case studies published by Siemens, which sells the simulation software involved, so treat them as company-reported results.

- **Wipro PARI (automotive machining/engine assembly):** The reported on-site commissioning reduction is 70%. The same project was also reported to have cut rework and delivery time. In addition to improving process reliability and resolving design and process issues early on, they reduced on-site commissioning time by 70 percent. A separate Siemens release says by incorporating VC with HiL, Wipro PARI minimized rework by 40 to 50 percent and reduced delivery time by 5 to 10 percent. Siemens' blog gives slightly different numbers for the machining line, saying rework fell as much as 50 percent and delivery time by as much as 10 percent. The 70% figure is the one repeated across the company's materials, and the case study also notes that a project could have been a six-to-eight-month job in normal conditions, which the company said was completed in three months.

- **Estun Automation (industrial robotics):** A Siemens blog post reports that the company uses Siemens Process Simulate software to reduce onsite virtual commissioning time by 30% and comprehensive commissioning costs by 20%.

Rockwell's FactoryTalk Design Studio Copilot is a generative AI assistant that writes PLC code from natural-language prompts. It was developed with Microsoft and runs in the cloud.

**What it does**
- Rockwell says the Copilot enables controls engineers to use natural language prompts for tasks like product guidance, code and ladder logic generation, code and ladder logic explanations, and troubleshooting.
- Its code generation is built on Microsoft Azure OpenAI Service.
- Rockwell's product page describes it simply: it uses Generative AI to process your natural language to help you create PLC code.
- A trade-press write-up describes a workflow where an engineer asks the Copilot to develop a pattern, and write ladder logic for me, and input certain parameters around a given process, like filling or cartoning or case packing. The operator can then continue to interact, refine, and add smart objects to get to a specified packaging process.
- Rockwell's more recent product page says users can use natural language prompts to model systems, generate PLC code, and resolve errors quickly.

**Smart Objects**
In Design Studio, code is organized into Smart Objects. One Copilot demo described building a Smart Object—a container of code—and then I can use it again and again in different places.

**Device management**
Rockwell says the Copilot can now handle device administration, including adding, removing, configuring, assigning, and unassigning devices. Rockwell claims this scales from managing 10 devices or 1,000.

**Platform and access**
- The tool runs in a browser. It is accessible through a web browser without downloads or installations and includes a collaborative, multi-user environment with integrated version control.
- It is controller agnostic, according to Control Global.
- Rockwell's controller support includes the ControlLogix 5590, which FactoryTalk Design Studio also now supports. The GuardLogix safety controllers are also supported, per Rockwell's Turkey and Belgium pages.

**Caveats**
The sources I found are mostly Rockwell marketing pages and trade-press coverage from the 2024 Automation Fair period, so I did not find independent evaluations of code quality or safety validation. Generated ladder logic should be reviewed and tested before it goes to a live machine. I also did not find pricing or licensing details. The LLM4PLC paper (Fakih et al., UC Irvine and Siemens) is an ICSE 2024 Software Engineering in Practice paper, and the search results describe its verification approach. The snippets say "SMV verifiers" but don't name NuSMV specifically, so I can't confirm from these results which model checker was used.

**Problem:** The authors argue that GPT-4 and LLaMa2 often fail to produce valid programs for PLC-controlled industrial control systems. The core issues are the lack of execution guarantees for generated code, poor explainability, and weak support for niche languages.

**Approach:** The authors propose a user-guided iterative pipeline that uses user feedback and external verification tools, including grammar checkers, compilers and SMV verifiers, to steer the LLM's generation. They also improve generation through prompt engineering and fine-tuning with LoRAs. The project's GitHub description frames it as a Model-Based Design approach that iteratively prompts LLMs to generate PLC code. A third-party summary adds that the LLM first produces a plan that breaks the specification into functions, variables, and finite state machine states, and then generates Structured Text code from it.

**Evaluation:** The authors tested GPT-3.5, GPT-4, Code Llama-7B, a fine-tuned Code Llama-7B, Code Llama-34B, and a fine-tuned Code Llama-34B using a FischerTechnik Manufacturing TestBed. The pipeline raised the generation success rate from 47% to 72%. The code quality scores differ between versions: the arXiv v1 preprint reports the Survey-of-Experts score rising from 2.25/10 to 7.75/10, while the ICSE listing reports from 3.0/10 to 7.2/10.

**Availability:** The authors released the experimental setup, the LLM fine-tuning weights, and video demonstrations on a dedicated webpage. The code and prompts are in the AICPS/LLM_4_PLC GitHub repository.

If you need to know exactly which model checker was used, the full paper is the place to confirm it.

The regulation's application date of 20 January 2027 is consistent across sources, and the software change is confirmed. Most results come from vendor sites, so check the official EUR-Lex text before relying on specifics.

**Application date**
- Regulation (EU) 2023/1230 becomes mandatory on 20 January 2027, per Pilz's guidance Application of the EU Machinery Regulation 2023/1230 is mandatory from 20 January 2027.
- Entry into force is dated differently across sources. One says it came into force in all member states on 19 July 2023, twenty days after it was published in the Official Journal of the European Union. Another gives the publication date as 29 June 2023.

**Software as a safety component**
- The definition of safety components now covers software. Per Drives and Controls, the definition of safety components now includes not only physical, digital and/or mixed-type components, but also software.
- Practically, this means software that performs a safety function on a machine is treated like any other safety component, which can affect conformity assessment.

**Related changes that often come with it**
- Substantial modifications: a machine changed in a way that affects CE compliance needs a new conformity assessment, and the party making the change becomes the manufacturer – with all the obligations that entails.
- Cybersecurity: Industrial Security is a mandatory element for the safety of machinery, and no longer open to the interpretation of those placing the machine on the market.
- Third-party certification: For the six listed product groups, machine manufacturers can no longer self-declare compliance in conjunction with a harmonized standard, as previously. Instead, a named accreditation body must be involved.

"""STOP/PROVE 36-month financial model. Standard library only.

Writes, in docs/business-plan/:
  model.csv   monthly model, one row per month (36 rows)
  README.md   only the tables between <!-- model:NAME:start/end --> markers are rewritten

Every number in the plan comes from the constants below. Change a constant,
re-run the script, and the CSV and the README tables stay consistent.
Amounts are USD. Month 1 = November 2026, the month after neatHack.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import re
from dataclasses import dataclass
from pathlib import Path

CSV_PATH = HERE / "model.csv"
README_PATH = HERE / "README.md"

# Calendar and currency
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
START_YEAR, START_MONTH = 2026, 11  # month 1 = Nov 2026
MONTHS = 36
INR_PER_USD = 95  # planning rate; the rupee traded near 96 per USD in Sep 2026
PRE_SEED_END = 15  # months 1-15 run on the pre-seed; the seed lands in month 16

    """Spending periods: P1 pre-seed, P2 first seed year, P3 scale-up."""

        return "P1"

        return "P2"
    return "P3"

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Model
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
def llm_run_cost() -> dict:
    """LLM cost of one verification run at Sonnet 5.5 list prices (year-1 cost index)."""
    p = RUN_PROFILE
    tokens_in = p["llm_steps"] * p["avg_context_tokens"]
    tokens_out = p["llm_steps"] * p["output_tokens_per_step"]
    parts = {
        "cache_read": tokens_in * p["cache_read_share"] * SONNET["cache_read"] / 1e6,
        "cache_write": tokens_in * p["cache_write_share"] * SONNET["cache_write_5m"] / 1e6,
        "uncached_input": tokens_in * p["uncached_share"] * SONNET["input"] / 1e6,
        "output": tokens_out * SONNET["output"] / 1e6,
    }
    base = sum(parts.values())
    return {
        "tokens_in": tokens_in,
        "tokens_out": tokens_out,
        "parts": parts,
        "base": base,
        "total": base * (1 + p["retry_overhead"]),
    }


def year_of(m: int) -> int:
    return (m - 1) // 12 + 1


def cost_per_run(m: int) -> float:
    return llm_run_cost()["total"] * LLM_COST_INDEX[year_of(m)]


def role_cost(role: Role, m: int, fallback: bool) -> float:
    if m < role.start or (fallback and not role.in_fallback):
        return 0.0
    if role.founder:
        seeded = (not fallback) and m > PRE_SEED_END
        return FOUNDER_MONTHLY["post_seed" if seeded else "pre_seed"]
    cost = float(role.monthly_usd)
    for rm in RAISE_MONTHS:
        if role.start < rm <= m:
            cost *= 1 + RAISE[role.location]
    return cost


def new_customers(m: int, fallback: bool) -> dict:
    if m <= 12:
        starter, team = Y1_NEW.get(m, (0, 0))
    elif fallback and m > PRE_SEED_END:
        starter, team = FALLBACK_NEW_AFTER_PRE_SEED
    else:
        starter, team = QUARTER_NEW[(m - 1) // 3 + 1]
    wins = FALLBACK_ENTERPRISE_WIN_MONTHS if fallback else ENTERPRISE_WIN_MONTHS
    return {"starter": starter, "team": team, "enterprise": 1 if m in wins else 0}


def simulate(fallback: bool = False) -> list[dict]:
    customers = {t: 0 for t in TIERS}
    churn_acc = {t: 0.0 for t in TIERS}  # fractional churn carried to the next month
    upgrade_acc = {t: 0.0 for t in UPGRADE_RATE}
    cash = 0
    prev_mrr = 0
    rows = []
    for m in range(1, MONTHS + 1):
        per = "P1" if fallback else period(m)

        # 1. Churn on the opening base (whole customers; fractions carry forward).
        churned = {}
        for t in TIERS:
            churn_acc[t] += customers[t] * MONTHLY_CHURN[t]
            churned[t] = int(churn_acc[t] + 1e-9)
            churn_acc[t] -= churned[t]
            customers[t] -= churned[t]
        churned_mrr = sum(churned[t] * PRICE[t] for t in TIERS)

        # 2. Upgrades (Starter -> Team, Team -> Enterprise).
        upgrades = {}
        for t, rate in UPGRADE_RATE.items():
            upgrade_acc[t] += customers[t] * rate
            upgrades[t] = int(upgrade_acc[t] + 1e-9)
            upgrade_acc[t] -= upgrades[t]
        for t, n in upgrades.items():
            customers[t] -= n
            customers[NEXT_TIER[t]] += n
        expansion_mrr = sum(n * (PRICE[NEXT_TIER[t]] - PRICE[t]) for t, n in upgrades.items())

        # 3. New customers.
        new = new_customers(m, fallback)
        for t in TIERS:
            customers[t] += new[t]
        new_mrr = sum(new[t] * PRICE[t] for t in TIERS)

        total = sum(customers.values())
        mrr = sum(customers[t] * PRICE[t] for t in TIERS)
        revenue = mrr  # billed monthly; annual prepayment would improve cash (not assumed)

        # 4. Cost of goods sold.
        runs = sum(customers[t] * RUNS_USED[t] for t in TIERS)
        llm = round(runs * cost_per_run(m))
        infra = round(runs * COMPUTE_PER_RUN + HOSTING_BASE + HOSTING_PER_CUSTOMER * total + PAYMENT_FEES * revenue)
        support = round(sum(role_cost(r, m, fallback) for r in ROLES if r.bucket == "cogs"))
        cogs = llm + infra + support
        gross_profit = revenue - cogs

        # 5. Operating expenses.
        payroll = round(sum(role_cost(r, m, fallback) for r in ROLES if r.bucket == "opex"))
        recurring = sum(v[per] for v in OTHER_OPEX.values())
        one_offs = sum(usd for (mm, _, usd, keep) in ONE_OFFS if mm == m and (keep or not fallback))
        commissions = 0
        if not fallback and m >= COMMISSION_START:
            commissions = round(COMMISSION_RATE * 12 * (new["team"] * PRICE["team"] + new["enterprise"] * PRICE["enterprise"]))
        other_opex = recurring + one_offs + commissions
        opex = payroll + other_opex

        # 6. Cash.
        burn = cogs + opex - revenue  # positive = cash out
        funding = (FALLBACK_FUNDING if fallback else FUNDING).get(m, ("", 0))[1]
        cash += funding - burn

        sm_payroll = sum(role_cost(r, m, fallback) for r in ROLES if r.dept == "S&M")
        ceo_half = 0.5 * role_cost(ROLES[0], m, fallback)
        sm_other = sum(OTHER_OPEX[k][per] for k in SALES_MARKETING_LINES)
        rows.append(
            {
                "month": m,
                "date": f"{START_YEAR + (START_MONTH - 1 + m - 1) // 12}-{(START_MONTH - 1 + m - 1) % 12 + 1:02d}",
                "period": per,
                "new_customers": sum(new.values()),
                "new_starter": new["starter"],
                "new_team": new["team"],
                "new_enterprise": new["enterprise"],
                "churned_customers": sum(churned.values()),
                "upgrades": sum(upgrades.values()),
                "starter_customers": customers["starter"],
                "team_customers": customers["team"],
                "enterprise_customers": customers["enterprise"],
                "total_customers": total,
                "arpa_usd": round(mrr / total, 2) if total else 0,
                "mrr_usd": mrr,
                "arr_usd": mrr * 12,
                "revenue_usd": revenue,
                "verification_runs": runs,
                "llm_cost_per_run_usd": round(cost_per_run(m), 3),
                "llm_cost_usd": llm,
                "infra_cost_usd": infra,
                "support_cost_usd": support,
                "cogs_usd": cogs,
                "gross_profit_usd": gross_profit,
                "gross_margin_pct": round(100 * gross_profit / revenue, 1) if revenue else "",
                "headcount": sum(1 for r in ROLES if r.start <= m and (r.in_fallback or not fallback)),
                "payroll_usd": payroll,
                "other_opex_usd": other_opex,
                "total_opex_usd": opex,
                "burn_usd": burn,
                "funding_usd": funding,
                "cash_usd": cash,
                "runway_months": round(cash / burn, 1) if burn > 0 else "",
                # Used for the summary tables only (not written to the CSV).
                "_churned_mrr": churned_mrr,
                "_expansion_mrr": expansion_mrr,
                "_new_mrr": new_mrr,
                "_prev_mrr": prev_mrr,
                "_commissions": commissions,
                "_sm_spend": sm_payroll + ceo_half + sm_other + commissions,
            }
        )
        prev_mrr = mrr
    return rows


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Output helpers
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
def usd(x: float, decimals: int = 0) -> str:
    sign = "-" if x < 0 else ""
    return f"{sign}${abs(x):,.{decimals}f}"


def usd_k(x: float) -> str:
    sign = "-" if x < 0 else ""
    x = abs(x)
    if x >= 1_000_000:
        return f"{sign}${x / 1e6:,.2f}M"
    return f"{sign}${x / 1e3:,.0f}k"


def pct(x: float, decimals: int = 0) -> str:
    return f"{100 * x:.{decimals}f}%"


def table(headers: list[str], rows: list[list], align: str | None = None) -> str:
    align = align or "l" + "r" * (len(headers) - 1)
    sep = ["---:" if a == "r" else "---" for a in align]
    lines = ["| " + " | ".join(headers) + " |", "| " + " | ".join(sep) + " |"]
    lines += ["| " + " | ".join(str(c) for c in row) + " |" for row in rows]
    return "\n".join(lines)


def tier_mix(r: dict) -> str:
    return f"{r['total_customers']} ({r['starter_customers']}/{r['team_customers']}/{r['enterprise_customers']})"


def gm(rows: list[dict]) -> float:
    rev = sum(r["revenue_usd"] for r in rows)
    return (rev - sum(r["cogs_usd"] for r in rows)) / rev if rev else 0.0


def nrr_trailing_12(rows: list[dict], end: int) -> float:
    """Approximate net revenue retention: product of monthly (1 - churn + expansion) on the opening base."""
    factor = 1.0
    for r in rows[end - 12 : end]:
        if r["_prev_mrr"]:
            factor *= 1 + (r["_expansion_mrr"] - r["_churned_mrr"]) / r["_prev_mrr"]
    return factor


def first_month(rows: list[dict], pred) -> int | None:
    return next((r["month"] for r in rows if pred(r)), None)


def month_name(m: int) -> str:
    names = "Jan Feb Mar Apr May Jun Jul Aug Sep Oct Nov Dec".split()
    idx = START_MONTH - 1 + m - 1
    return f"{names[idx % 12]} {START_YEAR + idx // 12}"


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# README blocks
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
def blocks(plan: list[dict], fb: list[dict]) -> dict[str, str]:
    out: dict[str, str] = {}
    run = llm_run_cost()
    by = {r["month"]: r for r in plan}
    years = {y: plan[(y - 1) * 12 : y * 12] for y in (1, 2, 3)}

    # Headline numbers
    fb_breakeven = first_month(fb, lambda r: r["month"] > 12 and r["burn_usd"] <= 0)
    plan_breakeven = first_month(plan, lambda r: r["month"] > 12 and r["burn_usd"] <= 0)
    pre_seed_burn = sum(r["burn_usd"] for r in plan[:PRE_SEED_END]) / PRE_SEED_END
    min_fb = min(fb, key=lambda r: r["cash_usd"])
    end = by[MONTHS]
    last3_burn = sum(r["burn_usd"] for r in plan[-3:]) / 3
    out["headline"] = "\n".join(
        [
            f"- **Pricing:** Starter {usd(PRICE['starter'])}/month, Team {usd(PRICE['team'])}/month, "
            f"Enterprise {usd(PRICE['enterprise'])}/month (modeled average; on-prem/VPC, quoted per site).",
            f"- **ARR:** {usd_k(by[12]['arr_usd'])} at month 12 ({month_name(12)}), {usd_k(by[24]['arr_usd'])} at month 24, "
            f"{usd_k(by[36]['arr_usd'])} at month 36; {by[12]['total_customers']} / {by[24]['total_customers']} / "
            f"{by[36]['total_customers']} paying customers.",
            f"- **Gross margin:** {pct(gm(years[1]))} in year 1, {pct(gm(years[2]))} in year 2, {pct(gm(years[3]))} in year 3 "
            f"(LLM cost per verification run {usd(run['total'], 2)} at Claude Sonnet 5.5 list prices in year 1).",
            f"- **Funding:** {usd_k(FUNDING[1][1])} pre-seed now (month 1); {usd_k(FUNDING[16][1])} seed in month 16 "
            f"({month_name(16)}) once the seed milestones below are met.",
            f"- **Runway:** pre-seed burn averages {usd_k(pre_seed_burn)}/month over months 1-15, so {usd_k(FUNDING[1][1])} "
            f"covers {FUNDING[1][1] / pre_seed_burn:.0f} months at that rate; {usd_k(by[PRE_SEED_END]['cash_usd'])} is still in the bank "
            f"when the seed is due. With the seed, cash bottoms at {usd_k(min(r['cash_usd'] for r in plan[PRE_SEED_END:]))} and "
            + (
                f"the company turns cash-flow positive in month {plan_breakeven} ({month_name(plan_breakeven)})."
                if plan_breakeven
                else f"month-36 cash of {usd_k(end['cash_usd'])} covers {end['cash_usd'] / last3_burn:.0f} more months "
                f"at the month 34-36 burn."
            ),
            f"- **If the seed slips:** freezing the team at {fb[PRE_SEED_END - 1]['headcount']} people and selling founder-led, "
            + (
                f"the company breaks even in month {fb_breakeven} ({month_name(fb_breakeven)}) with cash never below "
                f"{usd_k(min_fb['cash_usd'])}."
                if fb_breakeven
                else f"cash bottoms at {usd_k(min_fb['cash_usd'])} in month {min_fb['month']}."
            ),
        ]
    )

    # Pricing table
    out["pricing"] = table(
        ["", "Starter", "Team", "Enterprise"],
        [
            ["Price (USD / month)"] + [usd(PRICE[t]) for t in TIERS],
            ["Price (USD / year)"] + [usd(12 * PRICE[t]) for t in TIERS],
            ["Engineer seats"] + [SEATS[t] for t in TIERS],
            ["Active controller projects"] + [ACTIVE_PROJECTS[t] for t in TIERS],
            ["Verification runs included / month"] + [f"{RUN_ALLOWANCE[t]:,}" for t in TIERS],
            ["Expected runs used / month (model)"] + [f"{RUNS_USED[t]:,}" for t in TIERS],
            ["Overage per extra run"] + [usd(OVERAGE_PER_RUN, 2)] * 3,
            ["Monthly logo churn (model)"] + [pct(MONTHLY_CHURN[t], 1) for t in TIERS],
            ["Monthly upgrade to next tier (model)"]
            + [pct(UPGRADE_RATE["starter"], 1), pct(UPGRADE_RATE["team"], 1), "n/a"],
        ],
        "lrrr",
    )

    # LLM cost per run
    p = RUN_PROFILE
    tin = run["tokens_in"]
    parts = run["parts"]
    out["run-cost"] = table(
        ["Component", "Tokens per run", "Sonnet 5.5 price (USD / MTok)", "Cost per run"],
        [
            ["Prompt tokens read from cache", f"{tin * p['cache_read_share']:,.0f}", usd(SONNET["cache_read"], 2), usd(parts["cache_read"], 3)],
            ["Prompt tokens written to cache (5 min)", f"{tin * p['cache_write_share']:,.0f}", usd(SONNET["cache_write_5m"], 2), usd(parts["cache_write"], 3)],
            ["Uncached prompt tokens", f"{tin * p['uncached_share']:,.0f}", usd(SONNET["input"], 2), usd(parts["uncached_input"], 3)],
            ["Output tokens (incl. thinking)", f"{run['tokens_out']:,.0f}", usd(SONNET["output"], 2), usd(parts["output"], 3)],
            ["**Subtotal**", f"{tin + run['tokens_out']:,.0f}", "", f"**{usd(run['base'], 3)}**"],
            [f"Retries and failed steps (+{pct(p['retry_overhead'])})", "", "", usd(run["total"] - run["base"], 3)],
            ["**LLM cost per run, year 1**", "", "", f"**{usd(run['total'], 2)}**"],
            [f"Year 2 / year 3 (cost index {LLM_COST_INDEX[2]:.2f} / {LLM_COST_INDEX[3]:.2f})", "", "",
             f"{usd(run['total'] * LLM_COST_INDEX[2], 2)} / {usd(run['total'] * LLM_COST_INDEX[3], 2)}"],
            ["Compute: simulation, model checking, storage", "", "", usd(COMPUTE_PER_RUN, 2)],
        ],
        "lrrr",
    )

    # Unit economics per tier (year-1 costs)
    ue_rows = []
    for t in TIERS:
        llm = RUNS_USED[t] * run["total"]
        compute = RUNS_USED[t] * COMPUTE_PER_RUN
        fees = PAYMENT_FEES * PRICE[t]
        direct = llm + compute + fees + HOSTING_PER_CUSTOMER
        ue_rows.append(
            [TIER_LABEL[t], usd(PRICE[t]), usd(llm), usd(compute), usd(fees + HOSTING_PER_CUSTOMER), usd(direct),
             pct((PRICE[t] - direct) / PRICE[t]), pct((PRICE[t] - direct * (1 - (1 - LLM_COST_INDEX[3]) * llm / direct)) / PRICE[t])]
        )
    out["unit-economics"] = table(
        ["Tier", "Price / month", "LLM (year 1)", "Compute", "Hosting + payment fees", "Direct COGS / month",
         "Contribution margin, year 1", "Contribution margin, year 3"],
        ue_rows,
    )

    # Year-1 monthly revenue table
    y1 = []
    for r in years[1]:
        y1.append(
            [f"M{r['month']} ({month_name(r['month'])})", r["new_customers"], tier_mix(r), usd(r["arpa_usd"]), usd(r["mrr_usd"]),
             usd(r["cogs_usd"]), f"{r['gross_margin_pct']}%" if r["gross_margin_pct"] != "" else "n/a",
             usd(r["total_opex_usd"]), usd(r["burn_usd"]), usd(r["cash_usd"])]
        )

             usd_k(sum(r["cogs_usd"] for r in rs)), pct(gm(rs)), usd_k(sum(r["payroll_usd"] for r in rs)),
             usd_k(sum(r["other_opex_usd"] for r in rs)), usd_k(sum(r["burn_usd"] for r in rs)),

        ["Fallback without seed: break-even month", f"M{fb_breakeven} ({month_name(fb_breakeven)})" if fb_breakeven else "not within 36 months"],
        ["Fallback without seed: lowest cash", f"{usd(min_fb['cash_usd'])} in month {min_fb['month']}"],

    return out


def write_csv(rows: list[dict]) -> None:
    fields = [k for k in rows[0] if not k.startswith("_")]
    with CSV_PATH.open("w", newline="", encoding="utf-8") as fh:
        w = csv.DictWriter(fh, fieldnames=fields, lineterminator="\n")
        w.writeheader()
        for r in rows:
            w.writerow({k: r[k] for k in fields})


def update_readme(generated: dict[str, str]) -> list[str]:
    if not README_PATH.exists():
        return []
    text = README_PATH.read_text(encoding="utf-8")
    updated = []
    for name, body in generated.items():
        pattern = re.compile(
            rf"(<!-- model:{re.escape(name)}:start -->\n).*?(\n<!-- model:{re.escape(name)}:end -->)", re.S
        )
        text, n = pattern.subn(lambda m: m.group(1) + body + m.group(2), text)
        if n:
            updated.append(name)
    README_PATH.write_text(text, encoding="utf-8", newline="\n")
    return updated


def main() -> None:
    plan = simulate()
    fallback = simulate(fallback=True)
    write_csv(plan)
    generated = blocks(plan, fallback)
    updated = update_readme(generated)
    print(f"wrote {CSV_PATH.name} ({len(plan)} months)")
    print(f"README blocks updated: {', '.join(updated) if updated else 'none (no README markers yet)'}")
    for name, body in generated.items():
        print(f"\n## {name}\n\n{body}")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

"""STOP/PROVE 36-month financial model. Standard library only.

Run from the repo root:

    uv run python docs/business-plan/build_model.py

Writes, in docs/business-plan/:
  model.csv   monthly model, one row per month (36 rows)
  README.md   only the tables between <!-- model:NAME:start/end --> markers are rewritten

Every number in the plan comes from the constants below. Change a constant,
re-run the script, and the CSV and the README tables stay consistent.
Amounts are USD. Month 1 = November 2026, the month after neatHack.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import csv
import re
from dataclasses import dataclass
from pathlib import Path

HERE = Path(__file__).resolve().parent
CSV_PATH = HERE / "model.csv"
README_PATH = HERE / "README.md"

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Calendar and currency
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
START_YEAR, START_MONTH = 2026, 11  # month 1 = Nov 2026
MONTHS = 36
INR_PER_USD = 95  # planning rate; the rupee traded near 96 per USD in Sep 2026
PRE_SEED_END = 15  # months 1-15 run on the pre-seed; the seed lands in month 16


def period(m: int) -> str:
    """Spending periods: P1 pre-seed, P2 first seed year, P3 scale-up."""
    if m <= PRE_SEED_END:
        return "P1"
    if m <= 24:
        return "P2"
    return "P3"


PERIOD_LABEL = {"P1": "M1-M15 (pre-seed)", "P2": "M16-M24 (post-seed)", "P3": "M25-M36 (scale)"}

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Pricing and customers
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
TIERS = ("starter", "team", "enterprise")

RUNS_USED = {"starter": 60, "team": 300, "enterprise": 1_200}  # expected runs / customer / month
MONTHLY_CHURN = {"starter": 0.020, "team": 0.010, "enterprise": 0.005}  # logo churn per month

# Gross new customers per month. Year 1 is set month by month: (starter, team).
Y1_NEW = {4: (1, 1), 5: (1, 0), 6: (1, 1), 7: (2, 0), 8: (1, 1), 9: (2, 1), 10: (2, 1), 11: (1, 2), 12: (2, 1)}
# Months 13-36: (starter, team) new customers per month, by quarter (Q5 = months 13-15).
QUARTER_NEW = {5: (2, 2), 6: (2, 3), 7: (3, 3), 8: (3, 4), 9: (3, 4), 10: (4, 5), 11: (4, 5), 12: (5, 6)}
ENTERPRISE_WIN_MONTHS = (12, 15, 18, 20, 22, 24, 26, 27, 29, 30, 32, 33, 35, 36)

# Fallback scenario (seed does not close): founder-led sales only after month 15.
FALLBACK_NEW_AFTER_PRE_SEED = (2, 2)
FALLBACK_ENTERPRISE_WIN_MONTHS = (12, 15, 21, 27, 33)

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Cost of goods sold
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Claude Sonnet 5.5 list prices, USD per million tokens:
# https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/about-claude/pricing (read 2026-10-12)
SONNET = {"input": 2.00, "cache_write_5m": 2.50, "cache_read": 0.10, "output": 10.00}

# One verification run = one agent pass over one controller program and its twin:
# simulate scenarios, inject faults, analyse traces, patch, model-check, re-test, report.
RUN_PROFILE = {
    "llm_steps": 30,  # LLM calls (agent steps) per run
    "avg_context_tokens": 50_000,  # prompt size per step, averaged over the run
    "cache_read_share": 0.85,  # prompt tokens served from the prompt cache
    "cache_write_share": 0.10,  # prompt tokens written to the 5-minute cache
    "uncached_share": 0.05,  # prompt tokens billed at the base input price
    "output_tokens_per_step": 2_000,  # incl. thinking
    "retry_overhead": 0.20,  # failed steps, retries and re-runs
}
# Engineering target for cost per run (routing trace triage to Haiku, Batch API for
# nightly regressions). No vendor price cut is assumed.
LLM_COST_INDEX = {1: 1.00, 2: 0.80, 3: 0.68}
COMPUTE_PER_RUN = 0.05  # simulation + model-checker CPU + trace storage, USD per run

HOSTING_PER_CUSTOMER = 12  # USD per active customer per month
PAYMENT_FEES = 0.02  # share of revenue

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Team (fully loaded monthly cost in USD at start; India roles are CTC)
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
FOUNDER_MONTHLY = {"pre_seed": 2_000, "post_seed": 3_500}
RAISE = {"India": 0.08, "US": 0.04, "Germany": 0.04}  # applied in months 13 and 25
RAISE_MONTHS = (13, 25)


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Role:
    title: str
    location: str
    start: int
    monthly_usd: int
    bucket: str  # "opex" or "cogs" (customer-facing engineers are cost of revenue)
    dept: str  # R&D, S&M, G&A or CS
    founder: bool = False
    in_fallback: bool = False  # kept in the no-seed fallback scenario


ROLES = [
    Role("Co-founder & CEO (Mohammad Umar)", "India", 1, 2_000, "opex", "G&A", True, True),
    Role("Co-founder, engineering (Bilal Feroz Khan)", "India", 1, 2_000, "opex", "R&D", True, True),

    Role("Solutions / customer-success engineer #1", "India", 9, 1_600, "cogs", "CS", in_fallback=True),
    Role("Account executive #1", "US", 16, 10_000, "opex", "S&M"),
    Role("Senior ML / agent engineer", "India", 16, 3_200, "opex", "R&D"),
    Role("Controls engineer #2 (twin library)", "India", 17, 1_800, "opex", "R&D"),
    Role("Account executive #2 (DACH)", "Germany", 18, 9_000, "opex", "S&M"),
    Role("Solutions engineer #2", "US", 19, 9_000, "cogs", "CS"),
    Role("Product marketing / demand generation", "India", 20, 2_000, "opex", "S&M"),
    Role("Backend / platform engineer #2", "India", 22, 2_200, "opex", "R&D"),
    Role("Customer-success engineer #3", "India", 24, 1_600, "cogs", "CS", in_fallback=True),
    Role("Account executive #3", "US", 25, 10_000, "opex", "S&M"),
    Role("Formal methods engineer #2", "India", 26, 3_000, "opex", "R&D"),
    Role("Finance & operations manager", "India", 28, 1_800, "opex", "G&A"),
    Role("Solutions engineer #4", "Germany", 30, 8_500, "cogs", "CS"),
    Role("Frontend engineer", "India", 32, 2_000, "opex", "R&D"),
    Role("Partner / channel manager", "India", 34, 2_000, "opex", "S&M"),
]

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Other operating expenses (USD per month, by period) and one-off items
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
OTHER_OPEX = {
    "Software and tools (incl. PLC vendor licences)": {"P1": 800, "P2": 2_000, "P3": 3_500},
    "Office / co-working (India)": {"P1": 500, "P2": 1_500, "P3": 3_000},
    "Travel and trade shows": {"P1": 1_500, "P2": 6_000, "P3": 10_000},
    "Marketing and content": {"P1": 500, "P2": 4_000, "P3": 8_000},
    "Legal, accounting, compliance": {"P1": 1_000, "P2": 2_500, "P3": 3_500},
    "Insurance (product liability, E&O, cyber)": {"P1": 300, "P2": 1_500, "P3": 3_000},
    "Recruiting": {"P1": 0, "P2": 1_500, "P3": 2_000},
}
SALES_MARKETING_LINES = ("Travel and trade shows", "Marketing and content")
ONE_OFFS = [  # (month, item, USD, kept in the no-seed fallback)
    (1, "Incorporation and pre-seed legal", 5_000, True),
    (2, "PLC test lab: Siemens, Rockwell and Beckhoff starter kits and licences", 10_000, True),
    (16, "Seed round legal", 15_000, False),
    (17, "Test lab expansion: safety PLCs and drives", 12_000, False),
    (22, "SOC 2 Type I audit", 25_000, False),
    (30, "Independent functional-safety assessment of the tool", 40_000, False),
]
COMMISSION_RATE = 0.10  # of first-year contract value, new Team and Enterprise logos
COMMISSION_START = 16  # when the first account executive starts

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Funding
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
FUNDING = {1: ("Pre-seed", 500_000), 16: ("Seed", 3_000_000)}
FALLBACK_FUNDING = {1: ("Pre-seed", 500_000)}


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Model
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
def llm_run_cost() -> dict:
    """LLM cost of one verification run at Sonnet 5.5 list prices (year-1 cost index)."""
    p = RUN_PROFILE
    tokens_in = p["llm_steps"] * p["avg_context_tokens"]
    tokens_out = p["llm_steps"] * p["output_tokens_per_step"]
    parts = {
        "cache_read": tokens_in * p["cache_read_share"] * SONNET["cache_read"] / 1e6,
        "cache_write": tokens_in * p["cache_write_share"] * SONNET["cache_write_5m"] / 1e6,
        "uncached_input": tokens_in * p["uncached_share"] * SONNET["input"] / 1e6,
        "output": tokens_out * SONNET["output"] / 1e6,
    }
    base = sum(parts.values())
    return {
        "tokens_in": tokens_in,
        "tokens_out": tokens_out,
        "parts": parts,
        "base": base,
        "total": base * (1 + p["retry_overhead"]),
    }


def year_of(m: int) -> int:
    return (m - 1) // 12 + 1


def cost_per_run(m: int) -> float:
    return llm_run_cost()["total"] * LLM_COST_INDEX[year_of(m)]


def role_cost(role: Role, m: int, fallback: bool) -> float:
    if m < role.start or (fallback and not role.in_fallback):
        return 0.0
    if role.founder:
        seeded = (not fallback) and m > PRE_SEED_END
        return FOUNDER_MONTHLY["post_seed" if seeded else "pre_seed"]
    cost = float(role.monthly_usd)
    for rm in RAISE_MONTHS:
        if role.start < rm <= m:
            cost *= 1 + RAISE[role.location]
    return cost


def new_customers(m: int, fallback: bool) -> dict:
    if m <= 12:
        starter, team = Y1_NEW.get(m, (0, 0))
    elif fallback and m > PRE_SEED_END:
        starter, team = FALLBACK_NEW_AFTER_PRE_SEED
    else:
        starter, team = QUARTER_NEW[(m - 1) // 3 + 1]
    wins = FALLBACK_ENTERPRISE_WIN_MONTHS if fallback else ENTERPRISE_WIN_MONTHS
    return {"starter": starter, "team": team, "enterprise": 1 if m in wins else 0}


def simulate(fallback: bool = False) -> list[dict]:
    customers = {t: 0 for t in TIERS}
    churn_acc = {t: 0.0 for t in TIERS}  # fractional churn carried to the next month
    upgrade_acc = {t: 0.0 for t in UPGRADE_RATE}
    cash = 0
    prev_mrr = 0
    rows = []
    for m in range(1, MONTHS + 1):
        per = "P1" if fallback else period(m)

        # 1. Churn on the opening base (whole customers; fractions carry forward).
        churned = {}
        for t in TIERS:
            churn_acc[t] += customers[t] * MONTHLY_CHURN[t]
            churned[t] = int(churn_acc[t] + 1e-9)
            churn_acc[t] -= churned[t]
            customers[t] -= churned[t]
        churned_mrr = sum(churned[t] * PRICE[t] for t in TIERS)

        # 2. Upgrades (Starter -> Team, Team -> Enterprise).
        upgrades = {}
        for t, rate in UPGRADE_RATE.items():
            upgrade_acc[t] += customers[t] * rate
            upgrades[t] = int(upgrade_acc[t] + 1e-9)
            upgrade_acc[t] -= upgrades[t]
        for t, n in upgrades.items():
            customers[t] -= n
            customers[NEXT_TIER[t]] += n
        expansion_mrr = sum(n * (PRICE[NEXT_TIER[t]] - PRICE[t]) for t, n in upgrades.items())

        # 3. New customers.
        new = new_customers(m, fallback)
        for t in TIERS:
            customers[t] += new[t]
        new_mrr = sum(new[t] * PRICE[t] for t in TIERS)

        total = sum(customers.values())
        mrr = sum(customers[t] * PRICE[t] for t in TIERS)
        revenue = mrr  # billed monthly; annual prepayment would improve cash (not assumed)

        # 4. Cost of goods sold.
        runs = sum(customers[t] * RUNS_USED[t] for t in TIERS)
        llm = round(runs * cost_per_run(m))
        infra = round(runs * COMPUTE_PER_RUN + HOSTING_BASE + HOSTING_PER_CUSTOMER * total + PAYMENT_FEES * revenue)
        support = round(sum(role_cost(r, m, fallback) for r in ROLES if r.bucket == "cogs"))
        cogs = llm + infra + support
        gross_profit = revenue - cogs

        # 5. Operating expenses.
        payroll = round(sum(role_cost(r, m, fallback) for r in ROLES if r.bucket == "opex"))
        recurring = sum(v[per] for v in OTHER_OPEX.values())
        one_offs = sum(usd for (mm, _, usd, keep) in ONE_OFFS if mm == m and (keep or not fallback))
        commissions = 0
        if not fallback and m >= COMMISSION_START:
            commissions = round(COMMISSION_RATE * 12 * (new["team"] * PRICE["team"] + new["enterprise"] * PRICE["enterprise"]))
        other_opex = recurring + one_offs + commissions
        opex = payroll + other_opex

        # 6. Cash.
        burn = cogs + opex - revenue  # positive = cash out
        funding = (FALLBACK_FUNDING if fallback else FUNDING).get(m, ("", 0))[1]
        cash += funding - burn

        sm_payroll = sum(role_cost(r, m, fallback) for r in ROLES if r.dept == "S&M")
        ceo_half = 0.5 * role_cost(ROLES[0], m, fallback)
        sm_other = sum(OTHER_OPEX[k][per] for k in SALES_MARKETING_LINES)
        rows.append(
            {
                "month": m,
                "date": f"{START_YEAR + (START_MONTH - 1 + m - 1) // 12}-{(START_MONTH - 1 + m - 1) % 12 + 1:02d}",
                "period": per,
                "new_customers": sum(new.values()),
                "new_starter": new["starter"],
                "new_team": new["team"],
                "new_enterprise": new["enterprise"],
                "churned_customers": sum(churned.values()),
                "upgrades": sum(upgrades.values()),
                "starter_customers": customers["starter"],
                "team_customers": customers["team"],
                "enterprise_customers": customers["enterprise"],
                "total_customers": total,
                "arpa_usd": round(mrr / total, 2) if total else 0,
                "mrr_usd": mrr,
                "arr_usd": mrr * 12,
                "revenue_usd": revenue,
                "verification_runs": runs,
                "llm_cost_per_run_usd": round(cost_per_run(m), 3),
                "llm_cost_usd": llm,
                "infra_cost_usd": infra,
                "support_cost_usd": support,
                "cogs_usd": cogs,
                "gross_profit_usd": gross_profit,
                "gross_margin_pct": round(100 * gross_profit / revenue, 1) if revenue else "",
                "headcount": sum(1 for r in ROLES if r.start <= m and (r.in_fallback or not fallback)),
                "payroll_usd": payroll,
                "other_opex_usd": other_opex,
                "total_opex_usd": opex,
                "burn_usd": burn,
                "funding_usd": funding,
                "cash_usd": cash,
                "runway_months": round(cash / burn, 1) if burn > 0 else "",
                # Used for the summary tables only (not written to the CSV).
                "_churned_mrr": churned_mrr,
                "_expansion_mrr": expansion_mrr,
                "_new_mrr": new_mrr,
                "_prev_mrr": prev_mrr,
                "_commissions": commissions,
                "_sm_spend": sm_payroll + ceo_half + sm_other + commissions,
            }
        )
        prev_mrr = mrr
    return rows


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Output helpers
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
def usd(x: float, decimals: int = 0) -> str:
    sign = "-" if x < 0 else ""
    return f"{sign}${abs(x):,.{decimals}f}"


def usd_k(x: float) -> str:
    sign = "-" if x < 0 else ""
    x = abs(x)
    if x >= 1_000_000:
        return f"{sign}${x / 1e6:,.2f}M"
    return f"{sign}${x / 1e3:,.0f}k"


def pct(x: float, decimals: int = 0) -> str:
    return f"{100 * x:.{decimals}f}%"


def table(headers: list[str], rows: list[list], align: str | None = None) -> str:
    align = align or "l" + "r" * (len(headers) - 1)
    sep = ["---:" if a == "r" else "---" for a in align]
    lines = ["| " + " | ".join(headers) + " |", "| " + " | ".join(sep) + " |"]
    lines += ["| " + " | ".join(str(c) for c in row) + " |" for row in rows]
    return "\n".join(lines)


def tier_mix(r: dict) -> str:
    return f"{r['total_customers']} ({r['starter_customers']}/{r['team_customers']}/{r['enterprise_customers']})"


def gm(rows: list[dict]) -> float:
    rev = sum(r["revenue_usd"] for r in rows)
    return (rev - sum(r["cogs_usd"] for r in rows)) / rev if rev else 0.0


def nrr_trailing_12(rows: list[dict], end: int) -> float:
    """Approximate net revenue retention: product of monthly (1 - churn + expansion) on the opening base."""
    factor = 1.0
    for r in rows[end - 12 : end]:
        if r["_prev_mrr"]:
            factor *= 1 + (r["_expansion_mrr"] - r["_churned_mrr"]) / r["_prev_mrr"]
    return factor


def first_month(rows: list[dict], pred) -> int | None:
    return next((r["month"] for r in rows if pred(r)), None)


def month_name(m: int) -> str:
    names = "Jan Feb Mar Apr May Jun Jul Aug Sep Oct Nov Dec".split()
    idx = START_MONTH - 1 + m - 1
    return f"{names[idx % 12]} {START_YEAR + idx // 12}"


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# README blocks
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
def blocks(plan: list[dict], fb: list[dict]) -> dict[str, str]:
    out: dict[str, str] = {}
    run = llm_run_cost()
    by = {r["month"]: r for r in plan}
    years = {y: plan[(y - 1) * 12 : y * 12] for y in (1, 2, 3)}

    # Headline numbers
    fb_breakeven = first_month(fb, lambda r: r["month"] > 12 and r["burn_usd"] <= 0)
    plan_breakeven = first_month(plan, lambda r: r["month"] > 12 and r["burn_usd"] <= 0)
    pre_seed_burn = sum(r["burn_usd"] for r in plan[:PRE_SEED_END]) / PRE_SEED_END
    min_fb = min(fb, key=lambda r: r["cash_usd"])
    end = by[MONTHS]
    last3_burn = sum(r["burn_usd"] for r in plan[-3:]) / 3
    out["headline"] = "\n".join(
        [
            f"- **Pricing:** Starter {usd(PRICE['starter'])}/month, Team {usd(PRICE['team'])}/month, "
            f"Enterprise {usd(PRICE['enterprise'])}/month (modeled average; on-prem/VPC, quoted per site).",
            f"- **ARR:** {usd_k(by[12]['arr_usd'])} at month 12 ({month_name(12)}), {usd_k(by[24]['arr_usd'])} at month 24, "
            f"{usd_k(by[36]['arr_usd'])} at month 36; {by[12]['total_customers']} / {by[24]['total_customers']} / "
            f"{by[36]['total_customers']} paying customers.",
            f"- **Gross margin:** {pct(gm(years[1]))} in year 1, {pct(gm(years[2]))} in year 2, {pct(gm(years[3]))} in year 3 "
            f"(LLM cost per verification run {usd(run['total'], 2)} at Claude Sonnet 5.5 list prices in year 1).",
            f"- **Funding:** {usd_k(FUNDING[1][1])} pre-seed now (month 1); {usd_k(FUNDING[16][1])} seed in month 16 "
            f"({month_name(16)}) once the seed milestones below are met.",
            f"- **Runway:** pre-seed burn averages {usd_k(pre_seed_burn)}/month over months 1-15, so {usd_k(FUNDING[1][1])} "
            f"covers {FUNDING[1][1] / pre_seed_burn:.0f} months at that rate; {usd_k(by[PRE_SEED_END]['cash_usd'])} is still in the bank "
            f"when the seed is due. With the seed, cash bottoms at {usd_k(min(r['cash_usd'] for r in plan[PRE_SEED_END:]))} and "
            + (
                f"the company turns cash-flow positive in month {plan_breakeven} ({month_name(plan_breakeven)})."
                if plan_breakeven
                else f"month-36 cash of {usd_k(end['cash_usd'])} covers {end['cash_usd'] / last3_burn:.0f} more months "
                f"at the month 34-36 burn."
            ),
            f"- **If the seed slips:** freezing the team at {fb[PRE_SEED_END - 1]['headcount']} people and selling founder-led, "
            + (
                f"the company breaks even in month {fb_breakeven} ({month_name(fb_breakeven)}) with cash never below "
                f"{usd_k(min_fb['cash_usd'])}."
                if fb_breakeven
                else f"cash bottoms at {usd_k(min_fb['cash_usd'])} in month {min_fb['month']}."
            ),
        ]
    )

    # Pricing table
    out["pricing"] = table(
        ["", "Starter", "Team", "Enterprise"],
        [
            ["Price (USD / month)"] + [usd(PRICE[t]) for t in TIERS],
            ["Price (USD / year)"] + [usd(12 * PRICE[t]) for t in TIERS],
            ["Engineer seats"] + [SEATS[t] for t in TIERS],
            ["Active controller projects"] + [ACTIVE_PROJECTS[t] for t in TIERS],
            ["Verification runs included / month"] + [f"{RUN_ALLOWANCE[t]:,}" for t in TIERS],
            ["Expected runs used / month (model)"] + [f"{RUNS_USED[t]:,}" for t in TIERS],
            ["Overage per extra run"] + [usd(OVERAGE_PER_RUN, 2)] * 3,
            ["Monthly logo churn (model)"] + [pct(MONTHLY_CHURN[t], 1) for t in TIERS],
            ["Monthly upgrade to next tier (model)"]
            + [pct(UPGRADE_RATE["starter"], 1), pct(UPGRADE_RATE["team"], 1), "n/a"],
        ],
        "lrrr",
    )

    # LLM cost per run
    p = RUN_PROFILE
    tin = run["tokens_in"]
    parts = run["parts"]
    out["run-cost"] = table(
        ["Component", "Tokens per run", "Sonnet 5.5 price (USD / MTok)", "Cost per run"],
        [
            ["Prompt tokens read from cache", f"{tin * p['cache_read_share']:,.0f}", usd(SONNET["cache_read"], 2), usd(parts["cache_read"], 3)],
            ["Prompt tokens written to cache (5 min)", f"{tin * p['cache_write_share']:,.0f}", usd(SONNET["cache_write_5m"], 2), usd(parts["cache_write"], 3)],
            ["Uncached prompt tokens", f"{tin * p['uncached_share']:,.0f}", usd(SONNET["input"], 2), usd(parts["uncached_input"], 3)],
            ["Output tokens (incl. thinking)", f"{run['tokens_out']:,.0f}", usd(SONNET["output"], 2), usd(parts["output"], 3)],
            ["**Subtotal**", f"{tin + run['tokens_out']:,.0f}", "", f"**{usd(run['base'], 3)}**"],
            [f"Retries and failed steps (+{pct(p['retry_overhead'])})", "", "", usd(run["total"] - run["base"], 3)],
            ["**LLM cost per run, year 1**", "", "", f"**{usd(run['total'], 2)}**"],
            [f"Year 2 / year 3 (cost index {LLM_COST_INDEX[2]:.2f} / {LLM_COST_INDEX[3]:.2f})", "", "",
             f"{usd(run['total'] * LLM_COST_INDEX[2], 2)} / {usd(run['total'] * LLM_COST_INDEX[3], 2)}"],
            ["Compute: simulation, model checking, storage", "", "", usd(COMPUTE_PER_RUN, 2)],
        ],
        "lrrr",
    )

    # Unit economics per tier (year-1 costs)
    ue_rows = []
    for t in TIERS:
        llm = RUNS_USED[t] * run["total"]
        compute = RUNS_USED[t] * COMPUTE_PER_RUN
        fees = PAYMENT_FEES * PRICE[t]
        direct = llm + compute + fees + HOSTING_PER_CUSTOMER
        ue_rows.append(
            [TIER_LABEL[t], usd(PRICE[t]), usd(llm), usd(compute), usd(fees + HOSTING_PER_CUSTOMER), usd(direct),
             pct((PRICE[t] - direct) / PRICE[t]), pct((PRICE[t] - direct * (1 - (1 - LLM_COST_INDEX[3]) * llm / direct)) / PRICE[t])]
        )
    out["unit-economics"] = table(
        ["Tier", "Price / month", "LLM (year 1)", "Compute", "Hosting + payment fees", "Direct COGS / month",
         "Contribution margin, year 1", "Contribution margin, year 3"],
        ue_rows,
    )

    # Year-1 monthly revenue table
    y1 = []
    for r in years[1]:
        y1.append(
            [f"M{r['month']} ({month_name(r['month'])})", r["new_customers"], tier_mix(r), usd(r["arpa_usd"]), usd(r["mrr_usd"]),
             usd(r["cogs_usd"]), f"{r['gross_margin_pct']}%" if r["gross_margin_pct"] != "" else "n/a",
             usd(r["total_opex_usd"]), usd(r["burn_usd"]), usd(r["cash_usd"])]
        )
    out["revenue-y1"] = table(
        ["Month", "New", "Customers (S/T/E)", "ARPA", "MRR = revenue", "COGS", "Gross margin", "OpEx", "Net burn", "Cash"],
        y1,
    )

    # Quarterly table, years 2-3
    q = []
    for qi in range(5, 13):
        rs = plan[(qi - 1) * 3 : qi * 3]
        last = rs[-1]
        q.append(
            [f"Q{qi} (M{rs[0]['month']}-M{last['month']})", sum(r["new_customers"] for r in rs), tier_mix(last),
             usd(last["arpa_usd"]), usd(last["mrr_usd"]), usd_k(last["arr_usd"]), usd_k(sum(r["revenue_usd"] for r in rs)),
             pct(gm(rs)), usd_k(sum(r["burn_usd"] for r in rs)), usd_k(last["cash_usd"])]
        )
    out["revenue-quarterly"] = table(
        ["Quarter", "New", "Customers at end (S/T/E)", "ARPA", "MRR at end", "ARR at end", "Revenue", "Gross margin",
         "Net burn", "Cash at end"],
        q,
    )

    # Annual summary
    a = []
    for y, rs in years.items():
        last = rs[-1]
        a.append(
            [f"Year {y} (M{rs[0]['month']}-M{last['month']})", usd_k(sum(r["revenue_usd"] for r in rs)),
             usd_k(sum(r["cogs_usd"] for r in rs)), pct(gm(rs)), usd_k(sum(r["payroll_usd"] for r in rs)),
             usd_k(sum(r["other_opex_usd"] for r in rs)), usd_k(sum(r["burn_usd"] for r in rs)),
             usd_k(sum(r["funding_usd"] for r in rs)), usd_k(last["cash_usd"]), last["total_customers"],
             usd_k(last["arr_usd"]), last["headcount"]]
        )
    out["annual"] = table(
        ["Year", "Revenue", "COGS", "Gross margin", "Payroll (OpEx)", "Other OpEx", "Net burn", "Funding",
         "Cash at end", "Customers at end", "ARR at end", "Headcount at end"],
        a,
    )

    # SaaS metrics by year
    s = []
    for y, rs in years.items():
        new_logos = sum(r["new_customers"] for r in rs)
        sm = sum(r["_sm_spend"] for r in rs)
        cac = sm / new_logos
        new_arpa = sum(r["_new_mrr"] for r in rs) / new_logos
        payback = cac / (new_arpa * gm(rs))
        start_arr = plan[(y - 1) * 12 - 1]["arr_usd"] if y > 1 else 0
        net_new_arr = rs[-1]["arr_usd"] - start_arr
        burn = sum(r["burn_usd"] for r in rs)
        nrr = pct(nrr_trailing_12(plan, y * 12)) if y > 1 else "n/a (no 12-month base yet)"
        s.append([f"Year {y}", usd_k(net_new_arr), f"{burn / net_new_arr:.1f}x" if net_new_arr > 0 else "n/a",
                  nrr, usd(cac), usd(new_arpa), f"{payback:.1f} months"])
    out["saas-metrics"] = table(
        ["Year", "Net new ARR", "Burn multiple", "Net revenue retention", "Blended CAC", "New-customer ARPA",
         "CAC payback"],
        s,
    )

    # Headcount plan
    h = []
    for i, r in enumerate(ROLES, 1):
        cost = (f"{usd(FOUNDER_MONTHLY['pre_seed'])} -> {usd(FOUNDER_MONTHLY['post_seed'])} from M{PRE_SEED_END + 1}"
                if r.founder else usd(r.monthly_usd))
        inr = (f"{FOUNDER_MONTHLY['pre_seed'] * 12 * INR_PER_USD / 1e5:.1f} -> {FOUNDER_MONTHLY['post_seed'] * 12 * INR_PER_USD / 1e5:.1f}"
               if r.founder else (f"{r.monthly_usd * 12 * INR_PER_USD / 1e5:.1f}" if r.location == "India" else "-"))
        bucket = "COGS" if r.bucket == "cogs" else "OpEx"
        h.append([i, r.title, r.location, f"M{r.start} ({month_name(r.start)})", cost, inr, f"{r.dept} / {bucket}",
                  "yes" if r.in_fallback else "no"])
    out["headcount"] = table(
        ["#", "Role", "Location", "Starts", "Loaded cost / month (USD)", "INR lakh / year", "Dept / bucket",
         "Kept if seed slips"],
        h,
        "rlllrrll",
    )

    # Other opex
    o = [[k] + [usd(v[p]) for p in ("P1", "P2", "P3")] for k, v in OTHER_OPEX.items()]
    o.append(["**Total recurring**"] + [f"**{usd(sum(v[p] for v in OTHER_OPEX.values()))}**" for p in ("P1", "P2", "P3")])
    one = [[f"M{mm} ({month_name(mm)})", item, usd(v), "yes" if keep else "no"] for (mm, item, v, keep) in ONE_OFFS]
    out["opex"] = (
        table(["Other OpEx, USD / month", PERIOD_LABEL["P1"], PERIOD_LABEL["P2"], PERIOD_LABEL["P3"]], o, "lrrr")
        + "\n\nOne-off items:\n\n"
        + table(["Month", "Item", "Amount", "Kept if seed slips"], one, "llrl")
        + f"\n\nSales commissions: {pct(COMMISSION_RATE)} of first-year contract value on new Team and Enterprise "
        f"logos from month {COMMISSION_START}, when the first account executive starts. Payroll rises "
        f"{pct(RAISE['India'])} (India) and {pct(RAISE['US'])} (US, Germany) in months {RAISE_MONTHS[0]} and {RAISE_MONTHS[1]}."
    )

    # Funding and runway
    f = [
        ["Pre-seed (SAFE or CCPS)", f"M1 ({month_name(1)})", usd(FUNDING[1][1]),
         "3 founders + 4 hires in India, PLC test lab, design partners, first 20+ customers"],
        ["Seed", f"M16 ({month_name(16)})", usd(FUNDING[16][1]),
         "US and DACH sales, solutions engineers, SOC 2, functional-safety assessment, twin library"],
    ]
    plan_min = min(plan[PRE_SEED_END:], key=lambda r: r["cash_usd"])
    fb_end = fb[-1]
    runway_rows = [
        ["Average net burn, months 1-15", usd(pre_seed_burn)],
        ["Pre-seed runway at that burn", f"{FUNDING[1][1] / pre_seed_burn:.0f} months"],
        [f"Cash at month {PRE_SEED_END}, before the seed", usd(by[PRE_SEED_END]["cash_usd"])],
        [f"Peak monthly burn (plan)", f"{usd(max(r['burn_usd'] for r in plan))} in month {max(plan, key=lambda r: r['burn_usd'])['month']}"],
        ["Lowest cash after the seed (plan)", f"{usd(plan_min['cash_usd'])} in month {plan_min['month']}"],
        ["Cash at month 36 (plan)", usd(end["cash_usd"])],
        ["Burn at month 36 (plan)", usd(end["burn_usd"])],
        ["Runway at month 36 (plan, month 34-36 burn)",
         f"{end['cash_usd'] / last3_burn:.0f} months" if last3_burn > 0 else "cash-flow positive"],
        ["Fallback without seed: break-even month", f"M{fb_breakeven} ({month_name(fb_breakeven)})" if fb_breakeven else "not within 36 months"],
        ["Fallback without seed: lowest cash", f"{usd(min_fb['cash_usd'])} in month {min_fb['month']}"],
        ["Fallback without seed: ARR / cash at month 36", f"{usd_k(fb_end['arr_usd'])} / {usd_k(fb_end['cash_usd'])}"],
    ]
    out["funding"] = (
        table(["Round", "Timing", "Amount (USD)", "Use of funds"], f, "llrl")
        + "\n\n"
        + table(["Runway metric", "Value"], runway_rows, "lr")
    )
    return out


def write_csv(rows: list[dict]) -> None:
    fields = [k for k in rows[0] if not k.startswith("_")]
    with CSV_PATH.open("w", newline="", encoding="utf-8") as fh:
        w = csv.DictWriter(fh, fieldnames=fields, lineterminator="\n")
        w.writeheader()
        for r in rows:
            w.writerow({k: r[k] for k in fields})


def update_readme(generated: dict[str, str]) -> list[str]:
    if not README_PATH.exists():
        return []
    text = README_PATH.read_text(encoding="utf-8")
    updated = []
    for name, body in generated.items():
        pattern = re.compile(
            rf"(<!-- model:{re.escape(name)}:start -->\n).*?(\n<!-- model:{re.escape(name)}:end -->)", re.S
        )
        text, n = pattern.subn(lambda m: m.group(1) + body + m.group(2), text)
        if n:
            updated.append(name)
    README_PATH.write_text(text, encoding="utf-8", newline="\n")
    return updated


def main() -> None:
    plan = simulate()
    fallback = simulate(fallback=True)
    write_csv(plan)
    generated = blocks(plan, fallback)
    updated = update_readme(generated)
    print(f"wrote {CSV_PATH.name} ({len(plan)} months)")
    print(f"README blocks updated: {', '.join(updated) if updated else 'none (no README markers yet)'}")
    for name, body in generated.items():
        print(f"\n## {name}\n\n{body}")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

> An AI agent that commissions PLC control logic before it touches a real machine. It tests the program against a digital twin, finds safety and functional bugs, proposes restricted patches, **proves** the safety rules with a model checker, and hands the controls engineer a verified patch plus an auditable report.

Team **LastCommit** (Mohammad Umar, Bilal Feroz Khan, Fuad Ahamed) · India · pre-seed · built at neatHack 2026 · plan dated 12 Oct 2026. Month 1 of the model is November 2026. All amounts are USD; INR at a planning rate of ₹95/USD.

Every model number below comes from [`build_model.py`](build_model.py). The script writes [`model.csv`](model.csv) (36 monthly rows) and regenerates the tables in this file. The inputs for cfo.ai are in [`cfo-ai-inputs.md`](cfo-ai-inputs.md). Statements marked *assumption* are ours. Everything else links to a source.

## Headline numbers

<!-- model:headline:start -->
(generated)
<!-- model:headline:end -->

## 1. Problem

Controls engineers at system integrators and machine builders write ladder logic, then find its bugs during factory and site acceptance tests (FAT/SAT) or after start-up. Commissioning takes about **25% of machine development time**, and **15-18%** goes to debugging automation and control logic alone, according to German machine-tool-builder research [cited by Siemens](https://blogs.sw.siemens.com/simcenter/virtual-commissioning-training-for-automation-engineers/). The bugs that matter are the ones our demo seeds: an E-stop that resets without a deliberate restart, auto-restart after a guard door closes, timing races, and stuck sensors nobody supervises.

Finding bugs on site is expensive. Unplanned downtime costs the Fortune Global 500 about **$1.4 trillion a year (11% of revenue)**. An hour of downtime costs **$2.3M in automotive** and **$36k in FMCG** ([Siemens, *True Cost of Downtime 2024*](https://assets.new.siemens.com/siemens/assets/api/uuid:1b43afb5-2d07-47f7-9eb7-893fe7d0bc59/TCOD-2024_original.pdf)). Virtual commissioning tools help, but engineers still build the scenarios and judge the results by hand. Testing also shows only that the scenarios someone thought of pass. It does not show that a safety rule holds in every reachable state.

## 2. Customer

| Segment | Who signs | Why they buy | Entry tier |
|---|---|---|---|
| **System integrators** (10-200 controls engineers) | Engineering manager / owner | Fixed-price projects: every on-site day of logic debugging eats margin; FAT sign-off | Starter → Team |
| **Machine builders / OEMs** (packaging, conveyors, palletising, intralogistics) | Head of controls / R&D | Each machine variant needs re-commissioning; safety documentation for CE marking; warranty call-outs | Team → Enterprise |
| **Plant controls teams** (automotive, FMCG, logistics) | Plant engineering / reliability lead | Logic changes on running lines under management-of-change; downtime cost | Enterprise |

**Market.** PLC hardware is about an [$11.7B market](https://www.gminsights.com/industry-analysis/programmable-logic-controller-market). Virtual-commissioning software, our closest category, was about **$1.4B in 2025**, growing **13-15% a year** ([Precedence Research](https://www.precedenceresearch.com/virtual-commissioning-market), [Fact.MR](https://www.factmr.com/report/virtual-commissioning-market)). On buyer counts, estimates put established control system integrators in North America at over 1,200, and firms doing some integration worldwide at more than 4,000 ([Control Engineering](https://www.controleng.com/raising-the-bar-for-control-system-integrators/), [Control Engineering demographics](https://www.controleng.com/system-integrator-demographics/); these estimates are dated). Germany's machinery association VDMA alone has about [3,600 member companies](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Machinery_and_Equipment_Manufacturers_Association). *Assumption:* 10,000 reachable integrators, OEMs and plant teams in the US, DACH and India, at the model's month-36 blended contract value of about $22.8k a year, make a **~$230M ARR serviceable market**. The plan's month-36 ARR is about 1.5% of it.

## 3. Why now

1. **Agents can do the work.** Current LLMs read and edit control logic, call simulators and checkers as tools, and finish a 30-step run for about $1.50 with prompt caching (section 7). Research confirms the loop works. In [LLM4PLC](https://arxiv.org/abs/2401.05443) (ICSE 2024), adding verifier feedback to LLM-generated PLC code raised the success rate from 47% to 72%.
2. **Proofs are practical at machine scale.** A cell's control logic is a finite-state system. With timer abstraction, a model checker explores it exhaustively in seconds to minutes, so "it passed the tests" becomes "the rule holds in every reachable state, or here is the counterexample".
3. **Regulation.** The EU Machinery Regulation 2023/1230 applies from **20 January 2027** ([Pilz](https://www.pilz.com/en-PL/support/law-standards-norms/manufacturer-machine-operators/machinery-regulation)). Its definition of safety components now includes **software** ([Drives & Controls](https://www.drivesandcontrols.ca/changing-scenes/eu-machinery-regulation-2023-1230/)). Builders need evidence, not just test logs.
4. **More generated code.** Siemens ([Industrial Copilot for TIA Portal](https://www.automation.com/en-us/articles/april-2024/siemens-xcelerator-ai-industrial-copilot)) and Rockwell ([FactoryTalk Design Studio Copilot](https://www.oemmagazine.org/engineering/automation/article/22927841/rockwell-automations-factorytalk-design-studio-adds-generative-ai-copilot)) now generate PLC code from prompts. Code nobody wrote by hand needs independent verification.

## 4. Product and moat

**Input:** a digital twin of the machine, the control program (ladder rungs; IEC 61131-3 via PLCopen XML on the roadmap) and the safety rules. **The agent:** simulates scenarios and injects faults (stuck sensors, dropped signals, timing jitter), localises each failure, and proposes a *restricted* patch, editing only the rungs and operations the engineer allows. The engineer approves; nothing is deployed automatically. **Demo:** on a conveyor cell with 4 hidden seeded faults, the agent finds and fixes all 4 and proves 6 safety rules.

**Moat.**
- **Proof certificates and audit trail.** Once our reports are part of a customer's safety file and FAT protocol, switching means re-validating the process.
- **Twin and fault library.** Twins for conveyors, palletisers, packaging and robot cells, plus fault models, compound with every project.
- **Verified-fix data.** Every run produces (bug, patch, proof) triples, the training and evaluation data for a better agent.
- **Vendor-neutral integrations.** PLCopen XML, TIA Portal Openness, Studio 5000 L5X and TwinCAT. A vendor's copilot will not verify a rival's controller.
- **Independent assessment.** An independent functional-safety assessment of the tool (month 30) is slow and expensive for a newcomer to copy.

## 5. Competition

| Alternative | What it is | Public price | Gap STOP/PROVE fills |
|---|---|---|---|
| Siemens S7-PLCSIM Advanced, Process Simulate | Virtual PLC + 3D simulation (Siemens stack) | PLCSIM Advanced V5 ≈ [£3,282 per licence at RS](https://uk.rs-online.com/web/p/software/2674826); Process Simulate by quote | Engineers write the scenarios and judge the results; no fault finding, no proofs; Siemens only |
| Rockwell Emulate3D (+ Logix Emulate) | 3D emulation for Logix controllers | Quote | Same; Rockwell only |
| Beckhoff TwinCAT 3 simulation | Simulation inside TwinCAT | Engineering free; runtime licensed | Platform-specific simulation, no verification agent |
| Factory I/O | 3D training simulator | [Ultimate €278/yr or €765 one-off](https://factoryio.com/editions) | Training scenes; not a verification tool |
| realvirtual.io, Simumatik | Unity / cloud digital twins for virtual commissioning | [realvirtual Commercial €1,920/yr per developer](https://realvirtual.io/en/buy/); Simumatik subscription ([acquired by Virtualware, Oct 2024](https://www.preqin.com/data/profile/asset/simumatik-ab/728466)) | Better simulation, but the engineer still has to find the bugs |
| Code copilots (Siemens, Rockwell, ChatGPT, GitHub Copilot) | Generate and explain PLC code | Bundled / quote | Generate code but never prove it against a machine model |
| Model checkers (nuXmv, PLCverif) | Formal verification | Free / open source | Expert-only: no twin, no patch loop, no report a controls engineer can use |

We complement the simulators: a PLCSIM Advanced or Emulate3D model can serve as the twin, and we verify code written by people or by copilots.

## 6. Go-to-market

1. **Design partners (M1-M3).** Three unpaid pilots with Indian integrators and OEMs (packaging, conveyors), from the founders' network. Two convert in month 4.
2. **Founder-led sales (M4-M15).**
   - **Channels:** small US/EU integrators reached through bug-hunt videos backed by real neatlogs traces, r/PLC and PLCtalk, CSIA membership and webinars.
   - **Events:** Hannover Messe (Apr 2027) and SPS Nuremberg (Nov 2027).
   - **Self-serve:** Starter comes with a 14-day trial on sample twins.
3. **Sales team (M16+).**
   - **People:** a head of sales for North America, account executives in the US and DACH, and SDRs working US hours from India.
   - **Proof of value:** solutions engineers run 4-week proofs of value on one customer machine.
   - **Partners:** PLC-vendor marketplaces and partner programs, plus functional-safety consultancies as a referral channel.
4. **Land and expand.** Starter → Team (seats, projects) → Enterprise (site-wide, VPC/on-prem, safety evidence pack). Upgrades are in the model (1.5% of Starter and 0.5% of Team customers move up each month). Run overages are not.

## 7. Pricing

<!-- model:pricing:start -->
(generated)
<!-- model:pricing:end -->

All tiers include the verification report and neatlogs trace. Team adds the custom twin builder, proof certificates, Git/CI integration and SSO. Enterprise adds VPC or on-prem deployment (optionally on the customer's own Bedrock, Vertex or Azure LLM endpoint), the safety evidence pack and a named solutions engineer. The model bills everyone monthly at list price. Annual prepayment, discounts and overage revenue are left out.

**Why customers pay this.** A US controls engineer earns about [$92k](https://www.ziprecruiter.com/Salaries/Plc-Controls-Engineer-Salary), or [$125k median total pay](https://www.coursera.org/articles/controls-engineer-salary). Loaded at 1.3× over 1,800 hours, that is roughly **$80/hour** (*assumption*). In Germany an SPS programmer earns about [€57-59k](https://www.jobvector.de/gehalt/sps-programmierer/). In India, AmbitionBox puts a [PLC automation engineer at ₹4-15 lakh a year at 7 years' experience](https://www.ambitionbox.com/profile/plc-automation-engineer-salary).

- **Travel saved:** two fewer site days at $600 a day saves $1,200.
- **Total:** about **$2,800 per project**.

At that rate:
- **Team:** a customer running 2-3 projects a month saves $5.6k-8.4k a month, 2.8-4.2× its $2,000 price.
- **Starter:** one project a month is 5.6× its $500 price.
- **Enterprise:** one avoided hour of FMCG downtime ($36k) pays for almost five months of Enterprise.

<!-- model:run-cost:start -->

**Seed milestones (by month 15):**
- ≥ $400k ARR and ≥ 25 paying customers (the model has $426k and 27)
- The first Enterprise logo
- NRR ≥ 100%
- Measured LLM cost ≤ $1.50 per run
- Three referenceable case studies with defects found before site
- No safety-critical defect escaping a verified project

The India cost base keeps the pre-seed company close to default-alive. The fallback row shows break-even without the seed. The seed buys growth: month-36 ARR is about 2.2× the fallback's.

## 12. Risks and mitigations

| Risk | Mitigation |
|---|---|
| A missed bug contributes to an incident | Engineer sign-off on every patch; proofs scoped to the stated twin and rules; contracts cap liability; product-liability and E&O insurance from month 1; independent safety assessment (M30) |
| Twin fidelity: proofs on a wrong model | Validate twins against recorded I/O traces from the real machine; reusable validated components; held-out tests |
| PLC vendors bundle the same capability | Stay vendor-neutral and verification-first; integrate with vendor simulators instead of competing with them |
| LLM price, quality or outage | Allowances and overage pricing; caching, Haiku routing, Batch API; any Claude endpoint (Anthropic, Bedrock, Vertex, Azure); cost per run tracked in neatlogs |

| Small, India-based team selling to US/EU | Experienced US head of sales after the seed; integrator advisors; trade-show presence |

| Growth | New logos, MRR/ARR, ARPA, pilot → paid conversion, pipeline coverage |
| Retention | Logo churn, NRR, runs per active project, seats used |
| Efficiency and cash | Gross margin, CAC, CAC payback, burn multiple, net burn, months of runway |

   - **Proof of value:** solutions engineers run 4-week proofs of value on one customer machine.
   - **Partners:** PLC-vendor marketplaces and partner programs, plus functional-safety consultancies as a referral channel.
4. **Land and expand.** Starter → Team (seats, projects) → Enterprise (site-wide, VPC/on-prem, safety evidence pack). Upgrades are in the model (1.5% of Starter and 0.5% of Team customers move up each month). Run overages are not.

## 7. Pricing

<!-- model:pricing:start -->
(generated)
<!-- model:pricing:end -->

All tiers include the verification report and neatlogs trace. Team adds the custom twin builder, proof certificates, Git/CI integration and SSO. Enterprise adds VPC or on-prem deployment (optionally on the customer's own Bedrock, Vertex or Azure LLM endpoint), the safety evidence pack and a named solutions engineer. The model bills everyone monthly at list price. Annual prepayment, discounts and overage revenue are left out.

**Why customers pay this.** A US controls engineer earns about [$92k](https://www.ziprecruiter.com/Salaries/Plc-Controls-Engineer-Salary), or [$125k median total pay](https://www.coursera.org/articles/controls-engineer-salary). Loaded at 1.3× over 1,800 hours, that is roughly **$80/hour** (*assumption*). In Germany an SPS programmer earns about [€57-59k](https://www.jobvector.de/gehalt/sps-programmierer/). In India, AmbitionBox puts a [PLC automation engineer at ₹4-15 lakh a year at 7 years' experience](https://www.ambitionbox.com/profile/plc-automation-engineer-salary).

*Assumption*, worked example for a mid-size cell with 300 controls hours:
- **Debug hours:** logic debugging is 15-18% of the project, about 50 hours.
- **Hours saved:** removing 40% of it saves 20 hours (vendor case studies report 20-70% shorter commissioning, e.g. [70% at Wipro PARI](https://blogs.sw.siemens.com/tecnomatix/wipro-pari-reduces-commissioning-time-by-70/)). That is $1,600.
- **Travel saved:** two fewer site days at $600 a day saves $1,200.
- **Total:** about **$2,800 per project**.

At that rate:
- **Team:** a customer running 2-3 projects a month saves $5.6k-8.4k a month, 2.8-4.2× its $2,000 price.
- **Starter:** one project a month is 5.6× its $500 price.
- **Enterprise:** one avoided hour of FMCG downtime ($36k) pays for almost five months of Enterprise.

## 8. Unit economics and costs

**LLM cost per verification run.** A run is about 30 agent steps, with prompts averaging 50k tokens (program, twin, rules and tool definitions, mostly served from the prompt cache) and 2k output tokens per step. We price it at [Claude Sonnet 5.5 list prices](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/about-claude/pricing): $2 / MTok input, $2.50 cache write, $0.10 cache hit, $10 output.

<!-- model:run-cost:start -->

The year-2 and year-3 index is an engineering target, not a vendor price cut. It comes from two changes:
- Move trace triage and test generation to Claude Haiku 5.5 ($0.10 / $0.50 per MTok).
- Run nightly regression suites through the Batch API at 50% off.

These token counts are estimates. They will be replaced by measured tokens and cost per run from the hackathon's neatlogs traces (`docs/traces/`).

<!-- model:unit-economics:start -->
(generated)

Company gross margin is lower than per-tier contribution margin. COGS also includes base hosting and the solutions/customer-success engineers who onboard twins (headcount table, bucket COGS). Allowances cap the downside: a Team customer using all 500 runs still costs only about 38% of its price in LLM tokens.

## 9. Revenue projection

The drivers, all in `build_model.py`, are:
- **New customers:** a gross schedule per tier (months 1-3 are pilots).
- **Churn:** monthly logo churn of 2.0% / 1.0% / 0.5% (Starter / Team / Enterprise).
- **Upgrades:** the monthly upgrade rates in the pricing table.

Revenue equals MRR (billed monthly).

## 10. Operating costs and headcount

Engineering stays in India; sales and on-site solutions engineering are in the US and Germany. Costs are fully loaded (CTC for India roles).
