## 11. Funding and runway

<!-- model:funding:start -->
(generated)
<!-- model:funding:end -->

**Seed milestones (by month 15):**
- ≥ $400k ARR and ≥ 25 paying customers (the model has $426k and 27)
- The first Enterprise logo
- NRR ≥ 100%
- Measured LLM cost ≤ $1.50 per run
- Three referenceable case studies with defects found before site
- No safety-critical defect escaping a verified project

The India cost base keeps the pre-seed company close to default-alive. The fallback row shows break-even without the seed. The seed buys growth: month-36 ARR is about 2.2× the fallback's.

## 12. Risks and mitigations

| Risk | Mitigation |
|---|---|
| A missed bug contributes to an incident | Engineer sign-off on every patch; proofs scoped to the stated twin and rules; contracts cap liability; product-liability and E&O insurance from month 1; independent safety assessment (M30) |
| Twin fidelity: proofs on a wrong model | Validate twins against recorded I/O traces from the real machine; reusable validated components; held-out tests |
| PLC vendors bundle the same capability | Stay vendor-neutral and verification-first; integrate with vendor simulators instead of competing with them |
| LLM price, quality or outage | Allowances and overage pricing; caching, Haiku routing, Batch API; any Claude endpoint (Anthropic, Bedrock, Vertex, Azure); cost per run tracked in neatlogs |
| Customer IP (control code) leaves the plant | VPC / on-prem Enterprise; no training on customer code without consent; SOC 2 Type I (M22) |
| State-space explosion in model checking | Timer abstraction, per-station compositional checks, bounded checking with the bound stated in the report |
| Long industrial sales cycles | Self-serve Starter, design partners, integrators (who buy faster than plants), 4-week proofs of value |
| Small, India-based team selling to US/EU | Experienced US head of sales after the seed; integrator advisors; trade-show presence |

## 13. Metrics we track

| Area | Metric (source) |
|---|---|
| Agent quality | Seeded-fault detection rate; false-positive rate; % of runs ending in a verified patch; safety rules proven per run; held-out test pass rate (eval suite) |
| Agent operations | Tokens and LLM cost per run; steps per run; failed-action recovery rate; time to verdict (neatlogs traces) |
| Customer outcome (north star) | Logic defects caught before site per project; on-site debug hours saved (customer-reported) |
| Growth | New logos, MRR/ARR, ARPA, pilot → paid conversion, pipeline coverage |
| Retention | Logo churn, NRR, runs per active project, seats used |
| Efficiency and cash | Gross margin, CAC, CAC payback, burn multiple, net burn, months of runway |

# STOP/PROVE: business plan

> An AI agent that commissions PLC control logic before it touches a real machine. It tests the program against a digital twin, finds safety and functional bugs, proposes restricted patches, **proves** the safety rules with a model checker, and hands the controls engineer a verified patch plus an auditable report.

Team **LastCommit** (Mohammad Umar, Bilal Feroz Khan, Fuad Ahamed) · India · pre-seed · built at neatHack 2026 · plan dated 12 Oct 2026. Month 1 of the model is November 2026. All amounts are USD; INR at a planning rate of ₹95/USD.

Every model number below comes from [`build_model.py`](build_model.py). The script writes [`model.csv`](model.csv) (36 monthly rows) and regenerates the tables in this file. The inputs for cfo.ai are in [`cfo-ai-inputs.md`](cfo-ai-inputs.md). Market, price and salary figures link to their sources. Figures we estimated are marked *assumption*.

## Headline numbers

<!-- model:headline:start -->
- **Pricing:** Starter $500/month, Team $2,000/month, Enterprise $7,500/month (modeled average; VPC or on-prem, quoted per site).
- **ARR:** $216k at month 12 (Oct 2027), $1.37M at month 24, $3.38M at month 36, with 18 / 66 / 148 paying customers.
- **Gross margin:** 62% in year 1, 67% in year 2, 71% in year 3. LLM cost is $1.50 per verification run at Claude Sonnet 5.5 list prices in year 1.
- **Funding:** $500k pre-seed now (month 1), then a $2.00M seed in month 16 (Feb 2028) once the seed milestones are met.
- **Runway:** pre-seed burn peaks at $21k/month, so $500k is 24 months of runway at peak burn. Cash never drops below $340k before the seed. After the seed, burn peaks at $80k/month (month 22), cash bottoms at $1.59M (month 33), and the company is cash-flow positive from month 34 (Aug 2029), ending month 36 with $1.64M.
- **If the seed slips:** with the team frozen at 7 people and founder-led sales, the company is cash-flow positive from month 15 (Jan 2028) and cash never drops below $340k.
<!-- model:headline:end -->

## STOP/PROVE business plan: all four files are written, but none are committed yet

The first commit is stuck in Entire's git hook and is holding the worktree's `index.lock` (details under Commits). That lock also blocks the other session's git operations in this worktree.

### Headline numbers
All of these come from `build_model.py`.

- **Pricing** (billed monthly in the model):
  - Starter: $500/month, 2 seats, 100 runs included
  - Team: $2,000/month, 8 seats, 500 runs included
  - Enterprise: $7,500/month (about $90k/year), VPC or on-prem
  - Overage is $2.50 per run but is not counted in the model.
  - The ROI case is about $2,800 saved per machine project, using an assumed $80/hour engineer cost and 20 fewer debugging hours. That makes Team pay back 2.8–4.2× and Starter 5.6×.
- **ARR:**
  - Month 12 (Oct 2027): $216k, 18 customers
  - Month 24: $1.37M, 66 customers
  - Month 36 (Oct 2029): $3.38M, 148 customers
  - Net revenue retention is 107% in year 2 and 103% in year 3.
- **Gross margin:** 62% / 67% / 71% for years 1 / 2 / 3.
  - LLM cost is $1.50 per verification run. That assumes about 1.5M tokens over a 30-step run, priced at Claude Sonnet 5.5 list rates ($2 input, $2.50 cache write, $0.10 cache hit, $10 output per million tokens), plus 20% for retries.
  - The plan assumes cost per run falls by 20% in year 2 and 32% by year 3 through our own optimisation (Haiku routing, Batch API), not vendor price cuts.
- **Funding ask:** $500k pre-seed now (month 1, Nov 2026), then a $2M seed in month 16 (Feb 2028).
  - Seed milestones: at least $400k ARR (the model has $426k), at least 25 customers (27), and the first Enterprise customer.
- **Runway:**
  - Pre-seed burn peaks at $21k/month, so the pre-seed is 24 months of runway at peak burn. Cash stays at or above $340k before the seed.
  - After the seed, burn peaks at $80k/month, cash bottoms at $1.59M, and the company is cash-flow positive from month 34 (Aug 2029). It ends month 36 with $1.64M.
  - If the seed never closes: the team freezes at 7 people, the company is cash-flow positive from month 15, and ARR is $1.56M at month 36.
- **Headcount:** 7 at month 12, 19 at month 24, 30 at month 36. Engineering stays in India; sales and solutions engineers are in the US and Germany.

The README is about 1,670 words of prose plus tables, with sources linked inline. Figures we estimated are marked *assumption*. A script check confirmed the CSV's accounting adds up in all 36 rows.

### Files
- `C:\Users\omerj\Downloads\neathack-agent\.claude\worktrees\neathack-hackathon-e0846b\docs\business-plan\README.md`: the plan. Its tables are regenerated by the script between `<!-- model:NAME -->` markers, so the numbers cannot drift.

- `C:\Users\omerj\Downloads\neathack-agent\.claude\worktrees\neathack-hackathon-e0846b\docs\business-plan\model.csv`: 36 monthly rows and 33 columns, from month and customers through ARPA, MRR, revenue, COGS, payroll, burn, cash and runway.
- `C:\Users\omerj\Downloads\neathack-agent\.claude\worktrees\neathack-hackathon-e0846b\docs\business-plan\cfo-ai-inputs.md`: the checklist, also generated by the script. It covers timeline and funding events, plans with churn and upgrades, the new-customer schedule, COGS per customer, all 30 hires, other expenses and one-off costs, plus check numbers to compare against cfo.ai's output.

### Commits: none landed yet
- I ran `git commit -F - -- docs/business-plan/build_model.py docs/business-plan/model.csv` for "Add 36-month financial model for STOP/PROVE". It has been hung since 15:11 inside `entire.exe hooks git prepare-commit-msg` (process 81328; the parent git is process 95844).
- It holds `C:/Users/omerj/Downloads/neathack-agent/.git/worktrees/neathack-hackathon-e0846b/index.lock`.
- My attempt to stop the `entire.exe` process was denied, so I left it alone.
- The likely trigger is the commit with explicit paths. The other session's plain `git commit -m` commits went through.

**To unblock (user's decision):**
1. Stop only `entire.exe` (process 81328). The hook ends in `|| true`, so git then finishes commit 1 and releases the lock. Do not kill git itself; that would leave a stale `index.lock`.
2. Check `git diff --cached --name-only` shows nothing else staged.

4. Commit the checklist and the updated script: `git add docs/business-plan/build_model.py docs/business-plan/cfo-ai-inputs.md && git commit -m "Add cfo.ai input checklist generated from the model"`.
